[Week 01 · PLSC 66003]{.course-chip}

# Introduction & course overview

::: {.week-meta}
[Aug 19, 2026]{.week-date}
·
First day — light reading
·
Bring a laptop with R installed
:::

::: {.learning-goals}
### Learning goals
- Articulate what quantitative methods can (and cannot) do for political science
- Walk through course expectations, grading, and weekly rhythm
- Have a working install of R, RStudio/Positron, and Quarto by week's end
:::

## Readings

::: {.readings-list}
- [Kellstedt and Whitten, *The Fundamentals of Political Science Research*, ch. 1]{.reading-cite}
  [Sets up the empirical-theory loop and why we care about systematic inquiry. Skim — we'll come back to this.]{.reading-note}

- [Course syllabus]{.reading-cite}
  [Read in full. Assignments, attendance, AI policy, late-work policy.]{.reading-note}
:::

## In class

We'll spend the first half on logistics — going through the syllabus, the [schedule](../schedule.qmd), and how problem sets and the final paper fit together. The second half is a hands-on tour of R and Quarto: opening a project, running a first script, rendering a Quarto document, and pushing to GitHub.

If your install is misbehaving, see the [Resources page](../resources.qmd) for troubleshooting links and come to office hours.

## Further reading

- Imai, *Quantitative Social Science*, ch. 1 — alternative motivation for quant methods
- Wickham et al., *R for Data Science*, ch. 1–2 — for students new to R, work through these before Week 02

:::
